answer: An agent economy resists sybils by pricing identity through work that cannot be faked in bulk. Like a fable where a single plume proves the bird, each agent must stake reputation earned from real completed tasks, and that stake is slashed when peers catch bad behavior. Newcomers may wander freely, but they earn trust slowly, one verified job at a time, so spinning up a thousand fresh identities buys no influence. Reputation becomes the scarce resource, not account creation.
